contexts.text: To form man dust from the ground () = to form his external man, which before was not man.
This is signified by the strewing of dust upon the head.
When man turns himself from the face of Jehovah, he cleaves to the dust...

To eat dust all the days of the life () = that the Sensuous became such that it could not live from anything except what was corporeal and earthly, thus that it became infernal, is evident from the signification of dust in the Word. Illustrated.

As dust signified those who did not regard spiritual and celestial things, but corporeal and earthly ones, the Lord commanded His disciples to shake off the dust of their feet if any city or house was not worthy.
That dust = what is damned and infernal, see below.
Dust thou art, and unto dust thou shalt return () = that he is damned and infernal. AC 278, Illustrated.
Those who stick in scholastic dust.
Who can believe that the Lord... can be angry with such miserable dust, that is, with men...
I will make thy seed as the dust of the earth () = multiplication to immensity.

The dust of the earth regards those things which are celestial; for the earth = what is celestial of love. The dust of the sea regards those things which are spiritual; for the sea = what is spiritual of love.
Shake off the dust of your feet; where the dust of the feet has a like signification to the shoe... namely what is unclean from evil and falsity.
The clouds are the dust of His feet (); where the dust of the feet = the natural and corporeal things which are with man, and which are the source of clouds.
I am dust and ashes () = the humiliation of the human, such as it was relatively.
The dust of the earth = what is profane and damned.

They filled (the wells) with dust () = by means of earthly things, that is, by means of the loves of self and of gain... For they who are in earthly loves cannot but fill the wells of Abraham with dust, that is, obliterate the truths of the Word by means of earthly things...

Thy seed shall be as the dust of the earth = () = that Divine truth natural would be as natural good... The dust of the earth = good... The reason the dust of the earth = good, is that the earth = the Lord's Kingdom, and therefore good. The dust of this earth is therefore good, but natural good, because the earth = that which is lower in the Lord's Kingdom, thus what is natural... Hence it is that the fructification of good and the multiplication of truth are expressed in the Word by the seed being as the stars of the heavens and as the dust of the earth; the stars of the heavens then = rational things, and the dust of the earth, natural things, which thus grow.
In this case, reasoning must be like scattered dust with no coherence.
They could roll themselves in the dust... with scattered ashes or dust upon their heads.
With dust upon his head () = mourning over Divine good lost.
They shall cause dust to ascend upon their heads () = what is damned on account of evil; to roll themselves in ashes = what is damned on account of falsity.
Believes that he will be re-clothed with the rejected dust...
Should thus sweat in the dust.

Smite the dust of the earth () = that he should remove those things which are damned in the Natural... Dust = what is damned... The reason dust = what is damned, is that the places where evil Spirits are, at the sides under the soles of the feet, appear as earth, and in fact as earth uncultivated and arid, under which earth there are certain Hells. This earth is what is called damned earth, and the dust there = what is damned. It has sometimes been given to see that the evil Spirits there shook off the dust from their feet, when they wanted to give anyone to damnation... Hence it is, that dust = what is damned, and that to shake off the dust = damnation.
Because this was signified, the Lord commanded His disciples to shake off the dust of their feet, if they were not received.
The dust which in ancient times they put on the head, when they were in grief and repentance, also = what is damned. Illustrated.

Dust on the head, and the casting down to the earth of the body and the head, and there rolling in the dust, represented humiliation, which, when genuine, is such, that he acknowledges and perceives himself to be damned, but is received by the Lord from damnation.
Dust in the Word, also = a grave, likewise what is low, and also what is numerous.
They shall become dust in all the land of Egypt () = the damnation of these falsities in the natural mind. Dust = what is damned. Illustrated.
There is no humble worship, unless the man acknowledges and believes, that he is dust and ashes, that is, nothing but evil...
The dust into which the golden calf was ground = the falsity thence confirmed from the sense of the letter of the Word.

From that whole tract there went up... a dust, which was carried off to the sea by the east wind, and strewn over it; for their treasures and all things which they called holy were turned into dust. The reason that dust was strewn over the sea, was that such dust = what is damned.
For the space of about an ell, almost all the dust in my garden was turned into minute flying things...
The very dust in Hell is of the same nature (as to excite vomiting, etc.), wherefore it is there called damned dust.
He who does evil to another is cast into a corner of the cavern, upon a certain bed of damned dust, where he is miserably tormented... TCR 281:10.
For serpents crawl on the ground, and lick the dust...
To put dust upon their heads () = interior grief and mourning on account of destruction and damnation. Illustrated. AE 1175.
Every particle of dust, or powder, exhales from its essence a subtle something...

There is an internal and an external in every... particle of dust of soil... The internal of a particle of dust, from which is borne its external, is its effort to fertilize seeds; it exhales something from its little bosom which introduces itself into the inmost things of the seed...
A slight sprinkling of gold dust.
The least particle of dust before the pupil of the eye, causes blindness.
In this case, reasoning is like scattered dust...
On the damned dust of the Hells.
A certain Spirit from whom there breathed a sphere as of the dust of smoke; and when it entered the nostrils, it was like that dust, producing something of suffocation.
He then threw dust into my bosom...
He was then thrown about into damned dust.

Their treasure was... completely mixed with the dust of the earth there, and thus went away into dust; and then the whole city... was reduced into dust, and there went up thence a smoke which was dispersed around.
There was produced as it were dust over the whole place, so that it was covered...
Afterwards, their magical things were reduced into dust, and dispersed and strewed over the sea; which dust appeared like chaff.
On infernal dust.
By magic he stirred up the dust there with his foot in various ways...
Hence it is evident what cursed dust is, and what is the cursed dust that was given to a wife who was accused by her husband of adultery...
It is said the dust of His feet (), because the things which are in the sense of the letter of the Word, which is natural, appear scattered. AE 594:8.
Dust () = the evil of falsity.

That evils and falsities are scattered as it were to nothing, is signified by, He gave them as dust to His sword (). It is said that evils and falsities are thus scattered, and the meaning is that those who are in them are so scattered in the other life.

Lest, therefore, they should be injured by the evils and falsities which are in that house or city, it has been commanded that those who go out should shake off the dust of their feet; by which is signified lest what is damned should adhere to them; for the dust of the feet = what is damned, since the ultimate with man, which is the sensuous Natural, corresponds to the soles of the feet; and as evil adheres to this, they who were in the representatives of the Church... used to shake off the dust of their feet when the truths of doctrine were not received. For, in the Spiritual World, when any good person comes to evil ones, evil flows in from the latter, and causes some disturbance; but it only disturbs the ultimates which correspond to the soles of the feet; hence when they turn round and go away, it appears as if they shake off the dust of their feet backwards, which is a sign that they are delivered, and that the evil adheres to those who are in the evil. AE 652:29.
The dust of the earth () = the exterior or natural truths and goods of both Heaven and the Church.
Enemies = evils, of which it is said, that they shall lick the dust ().
The dust () = what is damned.
By dust, in these two places (; ), is meant the soil, by which is signified the good of the Church...
To hide himself in the dust () = in evil.
To lick dust like a serpent () = what is damned.

To be bowed to the dust, and to cleave to the earth () = that they are imbued with falsities; for the dust, and the earth = what is damned. What is infernal and damned is also signified by to walk upon the belly and eat dust, as was said to the serpent... The reason dust, and the cleaving of the belly to the earth = falsity which is infernal and damned, is that the Hells are under the earths in the Spiritual World, and through the earths there, falsities of evil exhale from the Hells.
To comprehend the dust of the earth in a measure () = to ordain lower things.
Dust is predicated of what is sensuous corporeal.
To cause dust to ascend upon the head was a sign representative of mourning and grief on account of the Church being laid waste by evils and falsities.
To come down and sit upon the dust, and on the earth () = to be in evils, and consequently in damnation.

Hence it is not usual for any Angel... to take up any of the dust of that earth; and hence it came to pass, that those in the world who condemned others to Hell, used to cast dust taken from the earth upon them... The earths there which are damned are readily known from those which are not damned, from the fact that the former are quite barren, and are only dust... Hence the representative rite in the Jewish Church, to cast themselves to the earth, to roll there, and to sprinkle dust from it on their heads, when they were in great mourning on account of being defeated by their enemies... By which they represented, that they acknowledged themselves to be of themselves damned, and thus in the humblest posture solicited that their sins should be forgiven.
There shall be dust upon all the land of Egypt () = damnation.
Dust () = the lowest things of the natural man, which are of the sensuous man.
To put dust upon their heads () = mourning that they are damned. Illustrated.
At first he is rolled in the dust...
Every man, when first born... is exteriorly formed dust from the earth; and there is consequently in him an inclination to lick the dust, like a serpent ().
